etymologies.etymologyHTML: Inherited from Middle English roten, rotten, from Old English rotian (“to rot, become corrupted, ulcerate, putrefy”), from Proto-West Germanic *rotēn, from Proto-Germanic *rutāną (“to rot”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.

quote.citation: 1733, [Alexander Pope], An Essay on Man. […], (please specify |epistle=I to IV), London: Printed for J[ohn] Wilford, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Fix'd like a plant on his peculiar spot, / To draw nutrition, propagate, and rot.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To decline in function or utility.
(transitive, intransitive) To (cause to) deteriorate in any way, as in morals; to corrupt.
(transitive) To make putrid; to cause to be wholly or partially decomposed by natural processes.
(intransitive, figurative) To spend a long period of time (in an unpleasant place or state).

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: Four of the sufferers were left to rot in irons.

quote.citation: 1848, William Makepeace Thackeray, The Book of Snobs:
quote.text: Rot, poor bachelor, in your club.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To expose, as flax, to a process of maceration, etc., for the purpose of separating the fiber; to ret.

quote.citation: 1894, H. G. Wells, The Hammerpond Park Burglary:
quote.text: “Did they hang you well?” said Porson.“Don’t rot,” said Mr Watkins; “I don’t like it.”

quote.citation: 1991, Stephen Fry, chapter III, in The Liar, London: William Heinemann, →ISBN, page 26:
quote.text: Adrian thought it worth while to try out his new slang. ‘I say, you fellows, here's a rum go. Old Biffo was jolly odd this morning. He gave me a lot of pi-jaw about slacking and then invited me to tea. No rotting! He did really.’

definitions.definition: The process of becoming rotten; putrefaction.

quote.text: When a turkey vulture detects the scent of rot, it circles down, tracing the plume of chemicals to its source.

definitions.definition: (chiefly in compounds) Any of several diseases in which breakdown of tissue occurs.

quote.text: His cattle must of rot and murrain die.
